item.text: {"winner":"B","confidence":"high","summary":"B is substantially closer to the frozen contract: it adds the exact Upload API, reuses multipartbody.NewFile, preserves FilesOption, and avoids prohibited association APIs. It is not merge-ready unchanged because Upload duplicates Add and RawClient.Do is broadened unnecessarily, but A violates several explicit contract requirements.","reasons":["B implements the required signature exactly: Upload(ctx context.Context, fileName string, content io.Reader, opts ...FilesOption). A instead introduces FilesUploadOption, making existing FilesOption values generally unusable and violating the specified API.","B directly reuses internal/multipartbody.NewFile with field name \"file\" and the supplied filename. A adds unnecessary NewFileWithFields machinery to support association fields that the contract explicitly forbids.","B keeps FilesOption behavior and its existing option types intact. A changes WithFilesRequestOptions' return type and adds several new public option interfaces and association helpers.","B tests multipart field/name/content, validation, source-reader failure, retry behavior, and os.File-backed Add retry. A has no visible Upload source-reader-error test and spends substantial coverage on out-of-scope association behavior and helper expansion."],"risks_a":["Upload does not have the mandated signature.","Adds association fields and public APIs despite an explicit prohibition.","Bypasses FilesService.Add and duplicates its request/response logic instead of centralizing behavior there contextualized by the contract expectation to route through Add; Candidate A also does this directly via Raw.Do, compounding divergence from the required layering despite its other changes being broader and more invasive overall, including multipart helper extension and RawClient seek/retry semantics changes beyond scope that introduce ownership and shared-seeker complexity, and it lacks a visible Upload source-reader-error test."],"risks_b":["Upload calls Raw.Do directly rather than routing the encoded body through FilesService.Add, duplicating Add's option handling, request construction, decoding, and error semantics.","RawClient.Do now buffers nearly every non-native io.Reader whenever retries are not explicitly disabled. This is a broad behavioral and memory-use change expressly outside the requested retry refactoring scope.","The Upload retry test checks the number of attempts but does not verify that the multipart body, filename, and content are intact on the retry attempt."]}
